extracted.intended_audience: historians / anthropologists / historical demographers estimating indigenous populations
extracted.subtask_description: Methods and evaluative principles for reconstructing aboriginal and mid-19th-century Native American population sizes (San Joaquin Valley region) using village lists, contemporary accounts, vaccination/tally records, archaeological/mission data, and extrapolation techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent estimates and average
rubrics_metrics.description: When several counts or estimates exist for the same area (e.g., Savage, Daily Alta letter, Johnston for Fresno–San Joaquin), take the average of the independent estimates as a working value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: three estimates of 2,700, ~3,000, and 2,200 (1,200+1,000) yielded an average of 2,633 for the Fresno–San Joaquin; use averages as one line of evidence but compare with other methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccination/list counts as population proxies (with corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use contemporary vaccination reports (e.g., Ryer's lists) and counts of vaccinations as a basis for estimating tribe or rancheria populations, but correct for indeterminate names, duplicates, and differences from blanket-distribution figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ryer's 4,451 vaccinations were corrected to 6,255 to conform to blanket distribution; then an average per tribe was computed (232), arbitrarily reduced to 200 to allow for nontribal/unrecognizable names; such adjustments must be documented and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Village-list (rancheria) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile village/rancheria counts from ethnographers and informants (Kroeber, Gayton, Latta, Merriam) and estimate average inhabitants per village to compute regional totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Village lists can be incomplete or biased; choose an appropriate average persons-per-village based on comparable areas (examples used: 53 from prorating Ryer, 70 as an intermediate figure, 100+ in some valley cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stream-mile (linear density) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive persons per stream mile from a well-documented subarea (North Fork Mono: population divided by stream miles) and apply that density to other river systems within the tribe's range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: North Fork had ~440 persons over ~60 stream miles = 7.33 persons/stream mile; applying this to 100 miles yielded 733 for a larger stretch. Use only when stream networks are comparable and tribal settlement correlated with streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area (areal density) method
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute persons per square mile from a baseline subtribe area and population, then scale to the total area of the group to estimate aggregate population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: North Fork area ~150 sq mi with 440 people, extrapolated to 1,090 sq mi gave 3,195. Compare results from stream-mile and area methods and assess plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct house/family counts for seasonal/rotational moves
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for repeated listing of the same family in village/site lists due to frequent moves; raw counts of houses or family-entries may overstate unique families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gifford's 227 families were reduced to 89 after accounting for repeats; identify recorded moves in appendices and apply proportional correction to unrecorded hamlets when reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use household/house-size conversions carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert number of houses to persons by applying an average persons-per-house value derived from ethnographic data (e.g., Gifford's 5 persons/house, or 6 persons per family for 'aboriginal standards').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the family/house size appropriate to the subtribe and time (e.g., valley settlements had larger averages than hill hamlets); document assumptions (examples: 5 persons/house, 6 persons/family).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select intermediate values when data conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: When different methods yield divergent values (e.g., village lists vs. vaccination counts vs. contemporary reports), adopt a compromise/intermediate estimate supported by reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for Fresno–San Joaquin the author chose an intermediate 70 inhabitants per village leading to 3,430, then compared with averages and vaccination-derived totals to settle on ~2,890 before adding Mono estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight contemporary accounts but beware systematic biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use contemporary pioneer, government, and treaty-attendance accounts as evidence but recognize they may undercount (only those seen at treaties/reservations) or overcount and may reflect post-contact decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preliminary estimate previously relied heavily on government officials and undercounted people not collected on reservations; cross-check with other sources and ethnographers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use archaeological and mission records for demographic structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mission baptism records and skeletal age distributions to estimate proportions of children and age-structure, enabling conversion of child counts into total population estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: mission censuses show under-10s ~21.4% (1782–1832); cemetery skeletons suggest 10–15% under-10; mission baptisms in two missions showed 17.8% children among 5,217 gentile baptisms—use these to infer total from reported numbers of children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer sample/region baselines when extrapolating to poorly documented groups
rubrics_metrics.description: When some subtribes lack comparable data, use a well-documented subtribe (e.g., North Fork Mono) as a baseline and extrapolate by villages, stream miles, or area—while noting potential density differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the baseline subtribe may be more or less dense than others; consider whether the group was unusually dense (North Fork possibly densest) and adjust or present ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply skepticism to extreme informant claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat very large or anomalous informant numbers (e.g., Wukchumne 'used to number' 5,000) with caution unless corroborated by other evidence; such claims may refer to earlier periods or be misremembered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inconsistent with documentary and other ethnographic evidence, downweight or reject extreme single-source figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple complementary methods and judge convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine village lists, vaccinations, contemporary counts, area/stream extrapolations, and archaeological/mission data; accept estimates where independent methods converge and explain discrepancies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author accepts totals when area comparisons, village lists, and contemporary accounts 'all apparently agree' (e.g., Kings–Kaweah estimated ~6,800).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for early contact-driven decline in interpreting 19th-century counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that Spanish/Mexican/early-American contact and introduced diseases had already reduced populations by the time of later observers; adjust 19th-century observed numbers when estimating precontact populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: mission and explorer records show continual decrease from 1770 onward; when estimating aboriginal (precontact) population, use earlier documentary evidence and correct for decline trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize place and tribal nomenclature before aggregating
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve inconsistent place and tribe names across sources (explorers and informants applied different names or the same name to different localities) before summing villages or population figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of duplicated names or name-application errors (Derby's confusion of Tachi and Chunut); cross-reference ethnographers and manuscript sources to align identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer detailed source-by-source consideration over gross aggregated counts
rubrics_metrics.description: A total derived from careful, detailed consideration of all available sources is preferable to one biased heavily by a particular class of sources (e.g., government treaty reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's final acceptance of 19,000 for San Joaquin Valley is justified by detailed subdivision analysis and cross-checking, deemed more reliable than the earlier 8,600 gross estimate.
